findings.obligation: Excluded-route set stays in step with the controllers that carry secrets (claim C3, design rule L2)
findings.observation: Logs and embed handshake prefixes are typed as literals ('new("/api/v1/logs")', 'new("/api/latest/embed/handshake")') next to the hub's shared constant, so a renamed controller route silently drops its exclusion; nothing but the unit rows guards the literals. Not a defect against the approved design (it prescribes this table); advice only.
findings.remediation: Optional follow-up: expose the logs and handshake route prefixes as constants on their controllers, as the hub does, and read them here.

findings.obligation: T6 and L2 oracle quality: marker must be checked by a reference the compiler holds, so a rename or removal of the attribute fails the build or test instead of reading as a missing string
findings.observation: Still looked up by name: 'private const string TheMarkerName = "Lighthouse.Backend.Platform.Host.NeverCompressResponseAttribute"' with the comment 'It is looked up by name until it exists; then it becomes typeof.' The type now exists, the comment is stale, and attribute.GetType() == markerType via Assembly.GetType(name) silently passes a null/renamed type only through the Is.True assertion.
findings.remediation: Replace the name lookup with typeof(NeverCompressResponseAttribute) (or IsDefined(typeof(...), false)) in both test classes, drop the stale comment and the markerType-null branch and the WHAT message's 'marker type found' part; the provider test's own marker-exists assertion at :136 becomes redundant.
